## Executive Summary

Phase 8 closed v2.0.0 — canonical naming won everywhere, the Dreams system is
structurally clean, and the AI triad coordination bus is live.

Phase 9 is the **Activity-First Protocol integration sprint**. The backend was
fully built (`lib/activity/`, `supabase/migrations/`, eight API routes, and six
UI components — see `docs/PHASE9_IMPLEMENTATION.md`). What is not yet done is
**wiring those systems into the actual surfaces users see and interact with**.

Every item below targets one of six integration priorities:

1. Wire ActivityProfile and TierBadge into the profile surfaces
2. Add SkipCreditBalance to the main navigation shell
3. Replace the engagement feed with the visibility-score feed
4. Connect ActivityPostForm to the post creation flow
5. Wire AdUnit into the content rendering path
6. Activate the IDARi PlatformHealth admin dashboard

This plan is surgical. No new tables. No new business logic. The algorithm
exists — it just needs to be connected to the surfaces that serve it.

---

## Priority 1 — Wire ActivityProfile and TierBadge into Profile Surfaces

The activity components exist in `components/activity/`. They are not yet rendered
anywhere in the profile surfaces. Profile visitors currently see no AQS, no
Real Shit Rate, and no tier badge. This is the highest-visibility gap.

---

### P1-A · `app/profile/[handle]/page.tsx` — Add ActivityProfile panel

**Current state:**

The page renders `ProfileWidgetGrid` with the standard bio/activity/followers
Dreams. There is no call to `ActivityProfile` or `TierBadge`. Users see no
activity data on their public profile.

**Why this matters:** `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §IV` mandates that user
profiles display Total Views, Activity Points (30-day), AQS, and Real Shit Rate.
These are the primary metrics — follower count must not be prominent.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// app/profile/[handle]/page.tsx
import ActivityProfile from '@/components/activity/ActivityProfile';
import TierBadge from '@/components/activity/TierBadge';

// Inside the page render, above ProfileWidgetGrid:
<div className="flex items-center gap-3 mb-4">
  <TierBadge userId={profile.id} />
  <ActivityProfile userId={profile.id} />
</div>
```

`ActivityProfile` fetches from `GET /api/metrics/user/[userId]`. No new data
fetching logic is needed in the page — the component handles it internally.

---

### P1-B · `app/edit-profiledream/page.tsx` — Add owner activity stats panel

**Current state:**

The EditProfileDream page shows the profile editor but no activity data for
the owner. Owners cannot see their own AQS or tier while editing.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// app/edit-profiledream/page.tsx — add above the widget editor section
import ActivityProfile from '@/components/activity/ActivityProfile';
import TierBadge from '@/components/activity/TierBadge';

// Inside the render, in the right sidebar or above the editor:
{user && (
  <div className="flex items-center gap-3 p-3 rounded-xl bg-white/5 mb-4">
    <TierBadge userId={user.id} />
    <ActivityProfile userId={user.id} />
  </div>
)}
```

---

### P1-C · `app/view-profile/page.tsx` — Include activity stats in preview

**Current state:**

ViewProfile preview renders the profile output. No activity stats are shown.
The owner's preview should mirror what a visitor would see on the public profile,
which now includes ActivityProfile and TierBadge per P1-A.

**Change required:**

Apply the same `ActivityProfile` + `TierBadge` block used in P1-A. The `userId`
is available from the server session. Components fetch their own data.

## Priority 2 — Add SkipCreditBalance to the Main Navigation Shell

The skip credit system is live on the backend. Users have no visibility into their
balance in the navigation shell. The `SkipCreditBalance` component exists at
`components/ads/SkipCreditBalance.tsx` and is not imported anywhere.

---

### P2-A · `components/menus/DualBottomMenu.tsx` — Add SkipCreditBalance to right panel header

**Current state:**

The DualBottomMenu renders the left (Daydreams) and right (DreamMenu) panels.
The right panel header shows the title but no balance indicator.

**Why this matters:** `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §V` specifies that skip
credits are earned by watching ads and auto-applied to skip future ads. If users
cannot see their balance, the incentive loop is invisible.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// components/menus/DualBottomMenu.tsx — in the right panel header
import SkipCreditBalance from '@/components/ads/SkipCreditBalance';

// Next to the "DreamMenu" panel title:
<div className="flex items-center justify-between px-3 py-2">
  <h2 className="text-sm font-semibold">DreamMenu</h2>
  <SkipCreditBalance />
</div>
```

---

### P2-B · `components/dreamengin/NexusMenu.tsx` — Add SkipCreditBalance to header row

**Current state:**

NexusMenu renders inside the Babylon scene. Its header shows "DreamMenu" but
no balance. Users in the 3D environment have no access to their credit balance.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// components/dreamengin/NexusMenu.tsx
import SkipCreditBalance from '@/components/ads/SkipCreditBalance';

// Next to the DreamMenu heading:
<div className="flex items-center justify-between px-2 py-1">
  <h2 className="text-sm uppercase tracking-[0.2em] text-white/60">DreamMenu</h2>
  <SkipCreditBalance compact />
</div>
```

Add a `compact` prop variant to `SkipCreditBalance` that shows only the number
and a coin icon with no label text, suitable for the Babylon overlay context.

## Priority 3 — Replace the Engagement Feed with the Visibility-Score Feed

`app/api/feed/route.ts` already has the `?sort=activity` parameter implemented
(per `docs/PHASE9_IMPLEMENTATION.md §3`). The feed surfaces still default to
the legacy engagement sort. The algorithm is live — it is not being called.

---

### P3-A · `app/homedream/page.tsx` — Switch default feed sort to `activity`

**Current state:**

The HomeDream page fetches the feed. The sort parameter is either absent or
set to the legacy default (not `activity`).

**Why this matters:** `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §III` mandates that feed
ranking uses the visibility score (`AQS × tier_multiplier + verification_strength +
innovation_bonus`). The engagement feed directly violates the core protocol.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// app/homedream/page.tsx — update the feed fetch call
const feedRes = await fetch(`/api/feed?sort=activity&limit=20`, {
  cache: 'no-store',
});
```

Or if the feed is fetched client-side in a component, update the query parameter
there. The `?sort=activity` flag is the only change needed — the server already
handles the rest.

---

### P3-B · Feed components — Remove like-count prominence, surface view-count

**Current state:**

Feed card components display like counts prominently. View counts are either
absent or secondary.

**Why this matters:** `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §IV` — "Feed: view count
prominent, no like count" is an explicit requirement.

**Change required:**

In the feed card component(s) (likely under `components/feed/` or `components/home/`):

```tsx
// Remove or deprioritize:
// <LikeCount count={post.likes} />

// Add or promote:
<ViewCount count={post.view_count} />
```

Like count can remain as a secondary indicator (small, muted) but must not be
the primary number shown on a post card.

---

### P3-C · `app/daydream/*/page.tsx` — Apply activity sort to Daydream feeds

The six canonical Daydream pages each have their own content feeds (music
tracks, code projects, games, etc.). All should apply the same `?sort=activity`
default to their internal feed calls for consistency with the core protocol.

## Priority 4 — Connect ActivityPostForm to the Post Creation Flow

`components/activity/ActivityPostForm.tsx` exists and renders a tier-aware post
form. It is not connected to the active post creation flow.

---

### P4-A · Identify and update the active post creation component

**Current state:**

The active post creation UI (likely in `components/home/`, `app/homedream/`, or
a DreamDM Bar compose surface) does not include tier selection or activity
verification. Posts are created without an activity tier being set.

**Why this matters:** `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §II` — every post has an
activity tier (0–6) that determines its point multiplier. Without tier selection
at creation time, every post defaults to Tier 0 (1× multiplier, no verification
bonus), which makes the reward system invisible to creators.

**Change required:**

Replace or wrap the existing post form with `ActivityPostForm`, or import its
tier-selection subcomponent into the existing form:

```tsx
// Wherever the active post composer renders
import ActivityPostForm from '@/components/activity/ActivityPostForm';

// Replace the existing compose UI or embed as a controlled component
<ActivityPostForm
  onSubmit={handlePost}
  userId={user.id}
/>
```

`ActivityPostForm` already calls `POST /api/activity/track` on submission. No
new API wiring is needed.

---

### P4-B · `app/api/feed/route.ts` — Ensure tier is stored with post on creation

**Current state:**

The feed post creation API (if any) may not persist the `activity_tier` field
alongside the post record.

**Change required:**

Verify that when a post is created (whichever endpoint handles it), the
`activity_tier` value from the form is persisted to the posts table. If the
column does not exist:

```sql
-- One-line migration addendum (append to existing migration or new file)
ALTER TABLE posts ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS activity_tier integer DEFAULT 0;
```

Then in the POST handler, include `activity_tier` in the insert payload.

## Priority 5 — Wire AdUnit into the Content Rendering Path

`components/ads/AdUnit.tsx` exists. It implements Pre-Roll, Post-Roll, and
Rewarded ad units with the skip credit earn system. It is not rendered anywhere
in the active content path.

---

### P5-A · `app/homedream/page.tsx` or feed component — Insert AdUnit at feed intervals

**Current state:**

The HomeDream feed renders posts with no ad units in the stream.

**Why this matters:** `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §V` defines three ad
placement types: Pre-Roll (before content), Post-Roll (after content), and
Rewarded (voluntary). The skip credit economy cannot function without ad placement.

**Change required:**

Insert a Rewarded AdUnit every N posts in the feed render (N = 5 is a reasonable
starting interval, tunable):

```tsx
// In the feed map:
{posts.map((post, idx) => (
  <>
    <PostCard key={post.id} post={post} />
    {(idx + 1) % 5 === 0 && (
      <AdUnit
        type="rewarded"
        userId={user?.id}
        onCreditEarned={() => {/* refresh balance */}}
      />
    )}
  </>
))}
```

---

### P5-B · `app/daydream/music/page.tsx` — Pre-Roll AdUnit before audio content

Per `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §V`, Pre-Roll ads play before content.
Music Daydream is the primary audio surface. Insert a Pre-Roll `AdUnit` before
the first track renders:

```tsx
<AdUnit type="pre-roll" userId={user?.id} contentId={track.id} />
<AudioPlayer track={track} />
```

The `AdUnit` component already handles skip credit earning and the `AD` badge
display. No new logic is required.

---

### P5-C · `app/api/views/track/route.ts` — Verify the route is called on content render

`POST /api/views/track` must be called each time a user views a post or piece of
content (not just clicks it). This is the data source for view-count-based ranking.

Audit all `PostCard`/`ContentCard` components and ensure they call this endpoint
on mount with an `IntersectionObserver` (50% visibility threshold) to record a
verified view.

## Priority 6 — Activate the IDARi PlatformHealth Admin Dashboard

`components/idari/PlatformHealth.tsx` exists. It displays Real Shit Rate,
Creation-to-Consumption Ratio, Outside Activity Rate, Average AQS, Ad View Rate,
and Harmful Content Rate. It is not wired into any admin route.

---

### P6-A · Create `app/admin/platform-health/page.tsx`

**Current state:**

No admin route surfaces the PlatformHealth component.

**Why this matters:** `docs/ACTIVITY_FIRST_PROTOCOL.md §IX` defines six success
conditions and requires IDARi to monitor platform health targets. The dashboard
exists but IDARi cannot access it.

**Change required:**

```tsx
// app/admin/platform-health/page.tsx
import { redirect } from 'next/navigation';
import { createServerClient } from '@/lib/supabase/server';
import PlatformHealth from '@/components/idari/PlatformHealth';

export default async function PlatformHealthPage() {
  const supabase = await createServerClient();
  const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  // Admin-only gate — adjust to your admin check
  if (!user) redirect('/login');

  return (
    <main className="p-6">
      <h1 className="text-2xl font-bold mb-6">Platform Health</h1>
      <PlatformHealth />
    </main>
  );
}
```

---

### P6-B · Add "Platform Health" link to the IDARi admin nav

If an admin navigation component exists (e.g. in `components/idari/` or
`app/admin/layout.tsx`), add a link to `/admin/platform-health`:

```tsx
<Link href="/admin/platform-health">Platform Health</Link>
```

## Execution Order

Each item is independently deployable. The ordering below minimises risk:
profile integrations first (low risk, high visibility), then navigation shell,
then feed algorithm, then creation flow, then ads, then admin.

| Order | ID | File(s) | Risk | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P1-A | `app/profile/[handle]/page.tsx` | Low | None — components self-fetch |
| 2 | P1-B | `app/edit-profiledream/page.tsx` | Low | None |
| 3 | P1-C | `app/view-profile/page.tsx` | Low | None |
| 4 | P2-A | `components/menus/DualBottomMenu.tsx` | Low | None |
| 5 | P2-B | `components/dreamengin/NexusMenu.tsx` | Low | SkipCreditBalance `compact` prop |
| 6 | P3-A | `app/homedream/page.tsx` (feed sort) | Low | None — endpoint ready |
| 7 | P3-B | Feed card components | Low | None |
| 8 | P3-C | `app/daydream/*/page.tsx` (6 pages) | Low | P3-A pattern established |
| 9 | P4-A | Active post composer | Medium | Identify correct composer component first |
| 10 | P4-B | Posts table migration + API | Medium | Requires Supabase migration |
| 11 | P5-C | PostCard IntersectionObserver | Medium | Views table migration already done |
| 12 | P5-A | HomeDream feed AdUnit intervals | Medium | P5-C (views tracked first) |
| 13 | P5-B | Music Daydream Pre-Roll | Medium | P5-A pattern established |
| 14 | P6-A | `app/admin/platform-health/page.tsx` | Low | None — component exists |
| 15 | P6-B | Admin nav link | Low | P6-A route created |

## What Phase 9 Does NOT Change

To be explicit about scope:

- No new database tables. The six tables from the Phase 9 migration are already
  created (`activity_points`, `activity_verification`, `views`, `skip_credits`,
  `ad_views`, `user_metrics`).
- No new business logic. `lib/activity/scoring.ts`, `lib/activity/aqs.ts`,
  `lib/activity/visibility-score.ts` are untouched.
- No changes to the AI triad (`lib/ai/`, `/api/ai/`).
- No changes to the Dream layer architecture (`components/dreams/`).
- No changes to the auth system or RLS policies.
- `docs/` files are not modified (read-only per Idari contract).
- The six canonical Daydream pages are not restructured — only their feed sort
  parameter and optional ad placement are updated.
- No follower count or like count is removed from the database — they are only
  deprioritised in display, as required by the protocol.
